Note::NlpAccessor::jaccard_terms¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::jaccard_terms(const Note& other) const

Content-Word Similarity Score Between Two Notes¶

jaccard_terms(other) is jaccard_tokens restricted to content words: it scores each cell pair by the Jaccard index of their significant-word sets, ignoring function words and short fillers. The result is a shape-preserving Float64 Note of native scores. The companion members for the same set are overlap_terms and intersect_terms.

How the score is computed¶

Each cell is tokenized and lowercased; a word joins the set only if it is 4 or more characters long and not a stopword (a, an, and, are, as, at, be, by, for, from, in, into, is, it, its, of, on, or, that, the, their, this, to, with). No stemming is applied. With sets A (from self) and B (from other), the score is |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B|, in [0, 1], symmetric.

Both sets empty (neither cell has a qualifying term) → 1.0. One empty and one not → 0.0. The default printer shows up to six decimals, trailing zeros trimmed (1.0, 0.5).

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

Per cell and pairwise; equal numel or a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast. Bytes-mode input raises Note::NlpAccessor::jaccard_terms requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs); a numel mismatch raises Note::NlpAccessor::jaccard_terms expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Only Content Words Count¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"The system processes documents"})
                 .nlp().jaccard_terms(pluss::make_note({"a system that processes files"}))
          << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, dtype=Float64)
[0.5]

the, a, and that are stopwords and drop out. The term sets are {system, processes, documents} and {system, processes, files} — two shared out of four distinct → 0.5.

See Also¶

  • Note::NlpAccessor::jaccard_tokens: the same score with no content filter.

  • Note::NlpAccessor::overlap_terms: the containment score over the same sets.

  • Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_terms: the shared terms themselves.
